entries.speaker: Yusuke
entries.en: If this is difficult for you, do not force[n]yourself to continue looking.

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: No, I'm okay.

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: The monster is gone now.

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: My real mom is with me... In my heart.

entries.speaker: Yusuke
entries.en: I see.

entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: Futaba's mom turned into this thing[n]'cause of what those shitty adults said[n]to her, right?

entries.speaker: Makoto
entries.en: Yes. When Futaba's cognition was[n]twisted by their words, the image of her[n]loving mother was distorted as well.

entries.speaker: Makoto
entries.en: That was truly reprehensible.

entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: Those bastards... How dare they stomp[n]all over a girl's heart like that?

entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: Sure am glad we managed to get her[n]back to normal.

entries.speaker: Shinya
entries.en: Is that... a sphinx!?

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: It appears so. Sphinxes are typically[n]stationed near tombs, serving as[n]guardian deities...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Look at how vengeful she is. What could[n]she have been trying to protect?

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: Futaba's cognition of her own mother[n]was twisted almost beyond recognition.

entries.speaker: Ann
entries.en: Kinda gives you an idea of what she[n]was going through...

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: Yeah.

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: It sounded unbearable. I can only[n]imagine how difficult that experience[n]must have been for her.

entries.speaker: Sumire
entries.en: Up there... That's a cognitive being,[n]right?

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: Yeah. If your heart gets warped enough,[n]your cognition can be so distorted that[n]even your own mother ends up like this.

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: It's a terrifying thought.

entries.speaker: Sumire
entries.en: Yeah...

entries.speaker: Sumire
entries.en: But I think it's even more terrifying that[n]there are people out there who could[n]make Futaba-senpai feel that way at all.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: So that's how you saw your mother[n]within your own heart...

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: Yeah... It's horrible. Even I think so.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Don't say that...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I can kind of relate. My image of my[n]father has been tainted as well.

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: Haru... It doesn't have to be that way.

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: The father who cared for you is still[n]there, deep in your heart. Don't let[n]those memories slip away.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: In my heart...

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: Er, sorry. I'm probably not making any[n]sense.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: No, I understand completely.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Thank you, Futaba-chan.

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: How does it feel to see that now, after[n]all the dust has settled? Does it ever get[n]any easier?

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: Well... I'd be lying if I said it did.

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: But I won't let it affect me anymore.[n]I've already decided to remember her[n]as the loving mom she really was.

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: Futaba...

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: Well said! That's what I like to hear[n]from a tried-and-true phantom thief!

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: Yeah!

entries.speaker: Sojiro
entries.en: Wakaba!? Could that really be her...?

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: No. Don't be silly, Sojiro.

entries.speaker: Futaba
entries.en: That thing is nothing like my mom. She[n]was way nicer, and WAY prettier.

entries.speaker: Sojiro
entries.en: R-Right...

entries.speaker: Sojiro
entries.en: Of course. The Wakaba I know was a[n]hundred times better than that.

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: What walks on four legs in the morning,[n]two legs in the afternoon, and three legs[n]in the evening?

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: That's what's known as the Riddle of[n]the Sphinx. Do either of you know the[n]answer?

entries.speaker: Ann
entries.en: Uh, what? Hmm...

entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: Oh, I know! It's a transforming robot!

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: Wrong. The correct answer... is man.

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: By the way, as the legend goes, the[n]sphinx would devour those who fail[n]her test.

entries.speaker: Kawakami
entries.en: So, you know. You may want to rethink[n]your study habits.

entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: Y-Yes ma'am...

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: That thing was nothing but a warped[n]cognition, but it still proved to be a[n]formidable foe.

entries.speaker: Ann
entries.en: Seriously. We only managed to beat it[n]because Futaba found the will to fight.

entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: Dude, she saved our asses with that uh...[n]What was it called? The arrow thing.

entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: Oh yeah, the barista!

entries.speaker: Ann
entries.en: That's a coffee shop employee!

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: I think he meant "ballista."
